M-A, M-B and M-C were judged on 10-20317 Hz, the drivers' own measured impedance sweeps (an impedance measurement has no gate), not on the chain's analysis grid (21-20000 Hz).
mid: its impedance sweep is narrower than the analysis grid, so the edges are held flat. Every electrical number outside its own sweep is an extrapolation.
tweeter: its impedance sweep is narrower than the analysis grid, so the edges are held flat. Every electrical number outside its own sweep is an extrapolation.
woofer: its impedance sweep is narrower than the analysis grid, so the edges are held flat. Every electrical number outside its own sweep is an extrapolation.
woofer: total series resistance bounded at 4.27 Ω, but no free series resistor carries it — the bound is reported and the gate enforces it.

woofer: the LF-lift bound of 2.72 mH is applied to the SUM of 2 free series coils, which is the quantity the metric sees. Each one is also capped at the total on its own — a necessary condition, not a second bound (V42).
mid: the series-capacitance pre-bound carries SLACK (A5d.6) — it shapes the search box and decides nothing; M-C is the authority on the f_s drive.

tweeter: the series-capacitance pre-bound (23.9 µF) would have excluded this design's own 31.4 µF. It carries SLACK, so it was widened to the design rather than applied — a pre-bound shapes the box and never condemns (A5d.6, casebook V12).

The LF-lift ceiling on woofer's series inductance is RE-SOLVED at the path resistance of the network being evaluated, not held at the 1.35 Ω the seed carried. The 2.72 mH above is therefore the ceiling at the START of the search and not the one it ended under (V48).

M-C (V50): a stated dB figure exists PER WAY for tweeter (-20 dB); every other protected way carries NO stated figure and is judged on the excursion-derived ceiling alone (or on nothing).

Upper-driver protection is judged by the STATED requirement — M-C at most the excursion-derived ceiling (V49), enforced by the gate at every point a pass accepts a network — and the full-band safety gate no longer compares against the seed. The two rules do not order the same designs: the seed comparison is stricter than the requirement on a well-protected seed and looser on a poor one (V47).

The amp-load barrier aimed at the |Z| minimum over 21-20000 Hz, 240 points — the tuner's own full-band safety grid, the one every other amp-floor reader has always used, through the same reader the M-B/|Z| gate takes its own minimum through. Goal and limit are therefore one question rather than two; where they can still differ is the grid, and that difference is measured against the floor slack rather than assumed away (V33).

The source-resistance probe read over 21-20000 Hz, 240 points — the tuner's own full-band safety grid and probed woofer at 51.5 Hz (its impedance peak — no box tuning was stated, so the probe took the peak; on a ported box that is a peak beside the tuning and not the tuning itself).

The dissipation term divided by the resolved R_e of woofer, 3.050 Ohm — the DC resistance the Q_es multiplication is defined on (A4 M-E), resolved once by the ingest pass and carried across the border rather than re-derived here.
